proposals.before: During Yongjia, the Prince of Langye first took post as General Who Guards the East and governed Yangzhou territory, and ordered Yu as army adviser.
proposals.after: During Yongjia, the Yuan Emperor first took post as General Who Pacifies the East and governed Yangzhou territory, and ordered Yu as army adviser.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 元帝, not the Prince of Langye; 安東將軍 is conventionally Pacifies/Calms the East rather than Guards the East.

proposals.before: When Shen Chong rose in revolt, Kong Yu quit his post for the capital, received appointment as Censor-in-chief, and advanced to palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.
proposals.after: When Shen Chong rose in revolt, Kong Yu quit his post for the capital, received appointment as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief, and advanced to palace attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.
proposals.reason: 御史中丞 is the Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief, not the Censor-in-chief (御史大夫).

proposals.before: He was soon shifted to senior minister of the masters of writing and offered General Who Guards the South and governor of Jiangzhou, but declined to assume the latter posts.
proposals.after: He was soon shifted to senior minister of the masters of writing and offered General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Jiangzhou, but did not take up those latter posts.
proposals.reason: 安南將軍 is General Who Pacifies the South, not Guards the South (鎮南); 不行 reports that he did not proceed to the posts.

proposals.before: At that time Ru Qianqiu through flattery won favor with the Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi; Wang repeatedly spoke of this to the emperor; the emperor did not adopt it.
proposals.after: At that time Ru Qianqiu through flattery won favor with the Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi; Wang repeatedly spoke of this to the emperor; the emperor did not adopt it.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 會稽王道子 is the Prince of Kuaiji named Daozi; 道子 is not the surname Wang. The literal line invents 'Wang Daozi'.

proposals.before: He was promoted to Minister of Education and Minister of Ceremonies; because it did not suit his wishes, he sought a post outside.
proposals.after: He was promoted to the masters of writing and minister of ceremonies; because it did not suit his wishes, he sought a post outside.
proposals.reason: 尚書 is the masters of writing, not Minister of Education (司徒). 尚書太常卿 has been mistranslated.

proposals.before: Promoted to the ministries of masters of writing and of ceremonies, he found the roles uncongenial and requested a provincial assignment.
proposals.after: Promoted to master of writing and minister of ceremonies, he found the roles uncongenial and requested a provincial assignment.
proposals.reason: 尚書太常卿 names offices (尚书 / 太常卿), not 'ministries' as institutions; the idiomatic line treats the titles as ministries.

proposals.before: The Huai River divides civilization from steppe folk; though north and south stand far apart, we gaze toward the Yellow River and ache for the Central Plains as thirst aches for water.
proposals.after: Hua and Di follow divergent ways; north and south stand far apart; gazing toward the River and longing for Song, we always ache as with hunger and thirst.
proposals.reason: 華狄 names the Hua and Di, not the Huai River; 企宋 is omitted in favor of an invented Central Plains.

proposals.before: In the first year of Sankan, Shi Cong raided Liyang; Wang Dao was grand marshal and campaigned against him; he requested Tan as marshal.
proposals.after: In the first year of Xiankang, Shi Cong raided Liyang; Wang Dao was grand marshal and campaigned against him; he requested Tan as marshal.
proposals.reason: 三康 is the era 咸康 (Xiankang); Sankan is not a standard rendering and contradicts the idiomatic 335 CE date.

proposals.before: Rescuing solar eclipse—if there is later mourning, heir apparent falls in well—then stop.
proposals.after: The rite to rescue a solar eclipse stops if there is mourning for an empress or if the heir apparent falls into a well.
proposals.reason: 後之喪 is mourning for the empress (后), not later mourning.

proposals.before: "Must a dying man sound like a fretful child?" Kong Tan snapped at Yu Bing. "Ask about the realm, not my bedside comfort!"
proposals.after: Kong Tan sighed and said: "When a great man nears his end, will you not ask about the arts that stabilize the state and pacify the household, and instead put on the questioning of girls and boys?"
proposals.reason: The Chinese rebukes the visitor for omitting statecraft questions; the idiomatic reverses the rebuke and invents a second line.

proposals.before: Xiū—short life—what is there to mourn!
proposals.after: Length or shortness is fate—what is there to mourn!
proposals.reason: 修短 is the pair long/short, not a name Xiū.

proposals.before: Restore ritual across the nine provinces, reunify the empire, raise victory monuments on the plain and bring the throne home to Luoyang—that was our shared dream.
proposals.after: Bring the nine domains to order, unify the four seas, raise a Jingguan mound on the Central Plain, and return the Purple Apex to the splendid soil—that was the old refrain and the root sincerity of our fervor.
proposals.reason: The Chinese does not name Luoyang.

proposals.before: Once someone lost wine and had just lifted it entering the gate; Yi from afar shouted at him: "Someone gifted me two jars of wine—why is one not so?"
proposals.after: Once someone brought him wine as a gift and had just lifted it entering the gate; Yi from afar shouted at him: "Someone gifted me two jars of wine—why is one not so?"
proposals.reason: The anecdote is a gifted present, not lost wine.

proposals.before: Clarify who leads armies and who guards the capital—like Han general versus Xiao He at home.
proposals.after: The court should further clarify appointments: Han Xin and Peng Yue may specialize in campaigns, while Xiao He and Cao Shen guard the bolts.
proposals.reason: 韓彭 and 蕭曹 are two named pairs; Peng Yue and Cao Shen are omitted.

proposals.before: Kong Yan and Yin He of Danyang argued: "The proper line is clear—close kin cannot be displaced; Emperor Ai ought to succeed Emperor Cheng."
proposals.after: Kong Yan and Yu He, governor of Danyang, argued: "Follow the root and dwell in the correct line; close kin cannot be displaced; he ought to be affiliated as successor of Emperor Cheng."
proposals.reason: 庾和 is Yu He, not Yin He; 繼 is ritual affiliation.

proposals.before: In Wukang two brothers' wives bore sons in the same famine; the younger brother, away on travel, told his wife to abandon their infant so her nephew might live.
proposals.after: In Wukang two brothers each had a pregnant wife; the younger brother had gone far and not returned; in a famine year they could not preserve both, so his son was abandoned and the elder brother's son kept alive.
proposals.reason: The Chinese does not say the absent brother instructed his wife.

proposals.before: At Ming Emperor's accession Ding Tan took chief commandant of attendant cavalry, court status, and the sacrifices bureau.
proposals.after: When the emperor (Yuan) ascended the throne, Ding Tan was appointed chief commandant of attendant cavalry, court attendant, and gentleman of the masters of writing bureau of sacrifices.
proposals.reason: Chinese 及帝踐阼 follows 元帝稱制 and precedes 太興三年; it is Yuan's AD 318 accession, not Ming Emperor.

proposals.before: When Prince Shou of Langye needed a chief minister, the throne favored Ding Tan and consulted He Xun.
proposals.after: When Prince Pou of Langye first received investiture, the emperor wished to draw court worthies as his state's senior minister and, about to use Tan, asked Director of the Palace Secretariat He Xun.
proposals.reason: The personal name is 裒 (Pou), not Shou; the unit also specifies first investiture and He Xun's office.

proposals.before: Grand General Wang Dun ordered him army adviser—shifted commandery administrative aide.
proposals.after: Grand General Wang Dun ordered him army adviser—shifted provincial administrative aide.
proposals.reason: Chinese 州別駕 is a provincial (zhou) aide, not a commandery post.

proposals.before: Liang did not heed."
proposals.after: Liang did not heed.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark with no opening quote in this unit.

proposals.before: Jun indeed came by Lesser Danyang through Moling—lost road—met commandery man—seized him as village guide."
proposals.after: Jun indeed came by Lesser Danyang through Moling—lost road—met commandery man—seized him as village guide.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark; this sentence is narrative, not a quotation.

proposals.before: At that time Jun marched by night—very without discipline."
proposals.after: At that time Jun marched by night—very without discipline.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark; this sentence is narrative.

proposals.before: Liang hearing deeply regretted not following Hui and others' words."
proposals.after: Liang hearing deeply regretted not following Hui and others' words.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark; this sentence is narrative.

proposals.before: With peace fragile Wang Dao named Tao Hui northern army inspector then Defender-in-Chief.
proposals.after: With peace fragile Wang Dao named Tao Hui northern army inspector then middle protector of the army.
proposals.reason: 中護軍 is the middle protector of the army, not 太尉 (commonly rendered Defender-in-Chief).

proposals.before: Named Defender-in-Chief while keeping prior titles, he died at fifty-one before inauguration.
proposals.after: Transferred to protector general while keeping prior titles, he died at fifty-one before inauguration.
proposals.reason: 護軍將軍 is protector general, not Defender-in-Chief.

proposals.before: The general-education scholar led armies; the colonel who pacified the Yue stood loyal and bright.
proposals.after: The Leader of the Army was refined and scholarly; the Pacifier of the Yue was loyal and bright.
proposals.reason: 領軍儒雅 contrasts office and character; 平越 is a title, not 'general-education scholar'.
